$comment: Phase 04 (196-section architecture + the 199-204 completeness addendum) resolved against repository artefacts. Four-way verified: architecture/phase-04-education-reality-engine.md, frontend/src/lib/kernel/phase-contracts/phase-04-reality-engine.ts, architecture/registry.json row 04, and the education/runtime code.

documentIntegrity.finding: The document was incomplete against the mandatory engineering sections (16/20; command, agent, observability, dependency, failure and data model absent). Owner instruction 2026-09-14: complete the architecture document, then build. An addendum (sections 199–204) was authored in the document's own style, stating existing behaviour rather than new scope; the audit now counts 20/20.

ownership.note: Phase 04 owns the educational reality model of an institution. It never owns identity (02), tenancy (03), devices (15), twins (16), automation (17), analytics (18), experience (24) or AI reasoning (26).

areas.requirement: Levels, programmes, curricula and versions, subjects, cohorts, classes and streams are modelled as typed reality objects, not hard-coded school structures.
An institution defines its own operating reality; the platform interprets that reality instead of dictating a structure.

areas.area: Persisted on the kernel reality substrate (§199)
areas.requirement: Reality objects are stored as cg_entity/cg_relationship/cg_observation/cg_event with tenant boundaries, not in a private store.
Every reality mutation is a server-side, validated, authorised, versioned command that fails closed.
Grading, assignment lifecycle and student progression are modelled with their own rules and evidence.
Buildings, facility capability, inventory and facility scheduling are represented and conflict-checked.
Language of instruction, multilingual delivery and localisation are modelled rather than assumed to be English-only.
The institution keeps operating without connectivity, on low bandwidth and with unreliable power.
Learning is represented as competency and mastery evidence, with student and teacher portfolios.

areas.area: AI is not the system of record; agent boundary (§117, §146, §201)
areas.requirement: AI interprets reality and proposes; only authorised commands make reality. Model output never overwrites canonical truth.

areas.area: Tenant isolation, authorization, privacy and child data protection (§134–§141)
areas.requirement: Reality is tenant-scoped, authorised server-side, and child data is protected with retention and audit obligations.
Reality changes emit versioned, tenant-tagged, idempotent domain events through the kernel outbox.

areas.area: Configuration validation, safe defaults and reality validator (§156–§163)
areas.requirement: An institution's configuration is validated and safe defaults applied; a reality validator detects impossible structures.
Reality models evolve without rewriting institutions: versioned curricula, migrations and blueprints.

areas.area: Engineering-section completeness of the phase document
areas.requirement: The document states the mandatory engineering sections (data model, command, agent, observability, dependency, failure) instead of leaving them implicit.

areas.area: Educational reality projected in a workspace (L4)
areas.requirement: The institution's operating reality is readable in a surface from real state, and the surface reports honestly when there is none.
areas.boundaryNote: Closed 2026-09-14: `/admin/education-reality` answers the phase's §1 questions from the institution's published operating model (own tenant only), rendering published/not_published/invalid_spec truthfully — it never renders a default school.
